analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: Equities bounced off significant overnight weakness, with a strong recovery in APAC tech. US broadening continued (SPW vs NDX more than +3.5% yesterday) while Europe lagged (SX5E broke its 200-day moving average).
Oil is higher and rates returned to safe-haven behavior. Gold failed to catch a bid and broke below $4000.

Equity markets are defined by two narratives: tech weakness and risk-off. On tech, the concern is financing, with capital the new AI bottleneck. META earnings did not relieve worries after it announced a new class of shares to facilitate future capital raises.
Risk-off signs include rotation into defensives, the US recession basket up 24% in 1 month, and a sharp rally in sovereign rates despite oil pressure. Global credit spreads reached 17-month highs.
Yesterday was the largest 1-day decline in UST yields since March 2023. Yields are increasingly correlated with NDX and negatively correlated with Brent.
France was singled out from the rates rally. The 10Y OAT-Bund spread widened 15bps on the day and is 55bps too wide on Research's sovereign risk framework, with no real catalyst for the selloff.
Catalysts to stabilise French spreads: swift budget approval, a broader EUR rates rally, ECB policy signalling or intervention, investor demand returning, and cleaner positioning/momentum turning.

Gilts were spared from the latest selling, but next week's UK budget is a key test. Research expects a fiscally neutral budget with no significant policy changes, a modest headroom increase and a small net financing requirement.

Global October flash PMIs are due today. Economists expect a retreat from September levels (which pointed to near 5% annualized growth), with the EU the key release (0.6pt drop forecast). Employment PMIs matter for Research's call for a labour market uplift.
Busy week ahead: Fed and ECB meetings, Mag7 earnings, and Brazil runoff elections on Sunday.

Tactically bullish on global equities. Regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU, because the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation and Asia has pockets of both.

Broadening can return, more clearly in the US than the EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but stability in EGB spreads is needed for conviction in EU broadening.

Longs: tech and supercycle themes (inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerable software), EU and Japan banks, EU industrials, Japan machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX, and selectively the consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerable names ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech and MDAX.

EM is bullish: it has recovered over 9% of the drawdown since the end-July bottom but remains off YTD highs. Drivers are global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, commodity broadening and scope for policy easing. Country-relative trades are preferred.
Positioning wrap: HF performance drawdown accelerated to -2.1% MTD globally from -0.8% the prior week. Eq L/S fell 2.3% MTD, quants 1% to 2%, multi-strats 2%, and APAC lagged most at -3.8% MTD.
Multi-strat de-grossing was close to the worst of the past 2 years. US positioning was around the 40th percentile, Europe the 11th and China/HK the 8th.

Despite neutral net positioning, the backdrop was fragile due to high gross, near multi-year-high 3-month flows into tech and extreme NDX long versus RTY short futures skews. AI Core Revenue positioning is at the 94th percentile (12m) and 99th (LT), and utilities remain heavily under-owned.

The current setup echoes 2023 more than 2018: US 10Y +82bps in 3Q26 vs +73bps in 3Q23, oil above +40% vs about +30%, quality outperforming beta. HFs are about +6% YTD and equities +13% MXWD / +14% SPX, a cushion that historically supports positive Q4 outcomes unless fundamentals deteriorate.
